35121-asbestos-its-production-and-use-wi:
Asbestos: Its Production and Use is a work on a strange mineral by Robert Jones, published in London in 1888. The preface is dated from a London hotel in April of that year. Jones calls asbestos one of nature's most marvellous products, a physical paradox. It is fibrous and crystalline at once, elastic yet brittle. It is a floating stone, he says, that can be carded, spun, and woven like cotton or silk. The book opens with its show at the American Exhibition.

The chief matter is where the stone is found and how it is worked. Italian and Canadian asbestos are compared at length. The mines of Canada get the fullest tale, group by group: Thetford, Coleraine, Broughton, Danville, and more. The uses of the fibre close the book. They run from fire-proof cloth to millboard and packing.
doe-osti-2574060-installation-and-commis:
Final technical report DE-SC0024254, prepared by C. Eric Dahl of Northwestern University and Fermilab and dated July 29, 2025, covers June 2023 to March 2025. The goal is a detector for sub-keV nuclear recoils, the faint kicks given off by light dark matter particles or by reactor antineutrinos scattering coherently off nuclei. The chosen technology is a bubble chamber filled with a superheated liquid noble gas, where a real recoil nucleates one bubble plus a flash of light.

Two thrusts made up the award. First, data from a prototype liquid xenon bubble chamber at Northwestern gave the first calibration of sensitivity at these low energies. Second, the ten-kilogram liquid argon chamber SBC-LAr10 was assembled and installed in the MINOS underground area at Fermilab. Backgrounds are expected below one event per ton-year. Precision calibration at Fermilab is the next step.
